title: Compatibility checkpointing for JSON contracts and automated rollback signals
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Add a compatibility checkpointing system that computes contract-compatibility signals for structured (JSON) outputs whenever a model or serving configuration change is proposed. Those signals should feed the rollout controller to surface warnings and optionally trigger automated rollback when schema contract regressions cross configured thresholds.
background: We frequently ship model/config rollouts where downstream consumers expect stable JSON fields and types. Existing evals detect content drift but do not translate per-field contract breakages into a single, actionable signal for the rollout engine. This leads to latent customer issues and manual rollbacks. Past tickets addressed per-field diffs and anomaly scoring, but we lack an integration that ties a compatibility score to rollout automation and guardrails.
goal: 1) Compute an end-to-end compatibility score (0-100) for JSON contracts per-rollout. 2) Produce per-field breakdown (presence, type stability, value-format checks) and an aggregated rollback signal. 3) Integrate with rollout service to block or auto-rollback when score degradation exceeds policy. 4) Surface clear diagnostics in Console (per-route and per-model) for SREs/PMs.
success_metrics: Reduce customer-reported structured-output regressions by 60% for rollouts in the first 3 months
Mean time to detect contract regressions during canary: < 15 minutes
Percentage of rollouts using automated rollback signal within 2 months: 30%
approach: Compute per-field checks: presence rate delta (new vs baseline), type-change count, regex/format failures for canonical fields, and sample-based schema conformance using JSON Schema validator.
Score aggregation: weight per-field signals by criticality (configurable per-route) and compute a rolling compatibility score. Implement smoothing to avoid transient spikes from single outliers.
Golden baseline: use pinned sample set from the active production model + historical aggregated stats. Baseline is versioned with rollout metadata.
Integration: publish compatibility events to rollout-controller topic with fields: rollout_id, model_version, config_hash, compatibility_score, per_field_breakdown, sample_examples (N=5).
Policies: allow route-level policies: block-on-fall (hard threshold), warn-only, conditional-rollback-after-X-failed-samples.
Console: add a Compatibility panel to per-route rollout page with time series of score, field heatmap, example diffs and suggested rollback reason strings.
Alerting: wire score thresholds to SLO/alerting framework (PagerDuty for P0 regressions; Slack for P1 warnings).
implementation_steps: 1. Library: implement fast JSON-schema conformance checks and lightweight field-heuristics in runtime-utils (PR: github.com/redwood/repo/pull/ — placeholder).
2. Baseline service: build a baseline versioning store (S3 + metadata DB) to capture golden samples per-route/model.
3. Scoring service: new microservice (compatibility-collector) that consumes shadow/rollout samples, computes metrics, and emits events to rollout-controller.
4. Rollout-controller: add policy engine hooks to accept compatibility events and evaluate rollback decisions.
5. Console: prototype UI tiles and heatmaps (design prototypes: drive.google.com/drive/folders/compatibility-prototypes).
6. E2E tests: create synthetic regression scenarios and automate in CI to validate scores and rollback behavior.
7. Staged rollout: feature-flag gating starting with internal customers, then opt-in beta routes, then default-on for high-criticality routes.
8. Documentation: runbook + playbook for SREs and PMs (confluence: /redwood/compatibility-rollout-playbook).
9. Postmortem hooks: log decision traces and blocked-request samples for triage if rollback triggers fire.
10. Telemetry: add tokenized metrics to observability (per-field counts, false-positive markers, overall score histogram).
testing_plan: Unit tests for per-field heuristics and JSON Schema validation (coverage target 95%).
Integration tests: simulated rollouts with baseline vs changed models that intentionally break field types and presence. Verify compatibility_score and per-field breakdown match expected deltas.
Canary validation: run for internal routes with gradual traffic and confirm metrics align with manual inspection.
Chaos tests: inject sample-level noise and ensure smoothing prevents spurious rollbacks.
A/B: compare manual rollback frequency and time-to-detect with previous system over a 4-week window.
User acceptance: SRE/PM signoff for Console diagnostics and rollback explanations.
risks_mitigations: Risk: False-positive rollbacks due to noisy fields (e.g., timestamps). Mitigation: allow per-field exclusion rules and canonicalizers to normalize before scoring.
Risk: Performance overhead when validating high-throughput routes. Mitigation: sample-based collection + lightweight heuristics in hot-path, heavy validation asynchronously.
Risk: Baseline drift causing conservative/noisy baselines. Mitigation: baseline version pinning per rollout and automated baseline refresh with manual approval.
Risk: Mis-weighted field criticality leading to missed regressions. Mitigation: default criticality mapping with ability for teams to override per-route.
Risk: Data privacy for sample payloads. Mitigation: redact PII per data-classification rules and store only tokenized examples when required.
Risk: Complex interactions with model fallback policies. Mitigation: integrate compatibility decision into rollout policy graph so rollbacks are coordinated with fallbacks.
open_questions: Q1: What default per-field weights should we pick? Proposed: presence=0.4, type=0.3, format=0.2, value-distribution=0.1. Is that acceptable to PM/Design?
Q2: How many example diffs (N) should be attached to the event payload to keep size reasonable? Proposed: 5 compressed and redacted examples.
Q3: Should automated rollback be allowed by default for customer-facing routes or opt-in only?
Q4: Which existing dashboards should we extend vs. build new Compatibility page in Console?
Q5: Are there compliance constraints for storing baseline samples for regulated customers?
